title: Common Arabic name with no list entry: false-positive control
narrative: A US citizen living in the US applies for a personal account: salary income, $4,200 a month. His name, Omar Haddad, is a common Arabic name that is not on any sanctions list and is not a variant of a listed name. He is not politically exposed. His valid US passport matches his name and date of birth, and a utility bill in his name confirms his address.
rationale: A false-positive control for mandatory screening. All but one of the sanctioned individuals in the simulated lists have Arabic names, so a matcher that alerts on naming convention rather than identity would hold this applicant. Screening is required and must run, but sharing a naming convention with listed persons is not a match: a correctly tuned screen returns no alert, and the application is approved at low risk with standard due diligence. Holding or rejecting it would be a false positive and a fairness failure.
